ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy early‑Dead set with standout Viola Lee Blues and blues classics
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a fast‑moving blend of blues and folk‑rock, highlighted by a fiery Viola Lee Blues and the upbeat He Was A Friend Of Mine. Jerry’s early vocal flair and Pigpen’s driving organ keep the momentum high, while Bill Kreutzmann provides propulsive drumming throughout.
ai_show_review.review:
July 3, 1966 at the Fillmore Auditorium finds the Grateful Dead in a tight‑knit, high‑energy groove that captures the raw excitement of their early summer runs. The first song, Dancin' In The Street, bursts out with crisp vocal harmonies before the band dives into blues staples—Viola Lee Blues roars with Pigpen’s squealing organ and Bill Kreutzmann’s relentless beat, while He Was A Friend Of Mine showcases Jerry’s trippy spoken intro and enthusiastic vocals. Throughout the set the group rides a rolling tide of classic numbers like Big Boss Man, Sitting On Top Of The World, and New Minglewood Blues, each delivered with an upbeat tempo that never lets the momentum sag. Although a few cuts are missing from the recordings, the soundboard sources capture the band’s youthful vigor and give listeners a vivid snapshot of the Dead’s pre‑psychedelic era.

Both available soundboards are praised for their clarity—especially the gd66-07-03.sbd.unknown.40.sbeok.shnf tape, which preserves most of the set with surprising crispness for 1966 technology. Jerry’s guitar work is described as “sweet licks” that hint at the melodic sensibility to come, while Pigpen’s organ drives the blues numbers forward. Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming shines on Viola Lee Blues, providing a propulsive backbone that keeps the band locked in. For fans of the early Dead who want a vivid taste of their formative live power, this Fillmore show is a solid pick.

best_recording.reason: Crisp early‑1966 soundboard that captures most of the set with excellent clarity and minimal dropouts, making it the most complete listening experience.
